pr_title: Dynamic update interval for Airly integration
pr_body:
<!--

## Breaking change
None


## Proposed change
In January 2020 Airly.eu changed terms of use of its API and now allows 100 requests per day (previously it was 1000 per day).
This PR change a way of update data from Airly. The update interval is calculated based on the number of configured Airly instances. If there is only one configured instance, the data will be updated every 15 minutes, two instances - update every 30 minutes, three instances - update every 45 minutes, etc. Integration uses DataUpdateCoordinator to update data via library.

issue_context.title: Airly refresh rate is too high and exceeds the API default daily requests limit
issue_context.body:

  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/

  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem

Currently default Airly API request limit per day is 100, which means we could do requests every 15 mins.
However, default refresh rate in homeasistant Airly integration is set to 10 mins.
This is causing that from ~6:30pm to 1am I don’t get any new Airly data as the rate limit is exceed and Airly API returns 429 code.

Ideally the refresh rate of how often the data is polled should be configurable/overridable, instead of a fixed value. This would resolve current issue and be helpful in case Airly lowers the limit again.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue: 0.107.2
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): 
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Raspbian Buster
- Integration causing this issue: Airly
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/airly/
